newsitem.title: FINLAND: Copper porphyry requires deft touch.
newsitem.headline: Copper porphyry requires deft touch.

text.p: Treatment of copper porphyry deposits require a careful balance of technologies for maximum recovery, Kenneth Stowe, vice president of operations at Canada's Westmin Resources, Ltd, said in a paper presented to a metal conference on Thursday.

Westmin's Gibraltar Mine in British Columbia has the distinction of being the lowest grade copper mine in North America but has stayed profitable by keeping up with technology, said the paper, presented at the Metal Bulletin Base Metal Concentrates Conference here.

"Mixing of oxide and sulphide ores has to be minimised if acceptable metallurgical performance is to be achieved," it said. "The ore must be blended on an ongoing basis to achieve the best compromise with respect to a number of variables including ore grade/mineral type, hardness and clay content."
Porphyry deposits have become the chief source of the world's copper, and are characterised by a huge mineral resource, relatively low grade and are at or near the surface.
Copper-gold porphyries pose a special problem because leaching technologies are limited, leaving flotation plants as the predominant technology for this type of deposit, he said.

Porphyries can feature four separate zones wtih vastly different metallurgical characteristics, requiring different techniques including cyanidation, acid leach or solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) and flotation.
"The development of a new leaching agent that could simultaneously extract both copper and gold would be a major impact," Stowe said.

The expense of off-site charges for copper concentrate transportation, smelting and refining -- usually $0.25-$0.35/lb -- is a big factor in the momentum towards heap leaching -SX-EW of sulphides despite the lower metal recovery rate, he said.
New on-site hydrometallurgical processes for sulphide concentrates are being actively researched by companies including Westmin, which would reduce transportation costs and increase metal recovery.
